# Local AI Development Environment

## Overview

This is a comprehensive local AI development environment designed for data analytics, FEM/Blender integration, energy optimization engines, and computer vision/ML applications on embedded devices.

The project runs local LLMs via Ollama and provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support for various systems including:
- Blender for 3D modeling
- FEniCS/Dolphin for finite element calculations  
- Graph optimization engines
- Computer vision (pose estimation)
- Knowledge graphs

## System Specifications

### Operating System
- **Distro:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
- **Kernel:** 7.0.0-22-generic

### CPU

| **Base Frequency** | Variable (417 - 5102 MHz boost) |

## Software Stack

### AI/ML Stack
- **Ollama:** ✓ Installed (local LLM serving)
- **CUDA:** ✓ Version 13.2
- **NVIDIA Drivers:** ✓ 595.71.05

### Development Tools
- **Python:** For AI/ML development (Python 3.10)
- **GCC/Clang:** For embedded development
- **Ansible:** For remote deployment (Jetson)
- **Docker:** For containerized services
- **FastAPI:** For web APIs
- **Gradio:** For web-based UI

## Project Components

### Main Development Areas

#### 1. FEM Analysis
- **Technology:** FEniCS, Dolphin
- **Use Case:** Heat transfer calculations
- **Directory:** `heat_fem/` (external project reference)

#### 2. Optimization Engine
- **Technology:** Graph-based optimization
- **Use Case:** Energy systems optimization
- **Directory:** `phys_opt/` (external project reference)

#### 3. Computer Vision
- **Technology:** Pose estimation, PyTorch vision models
- **Use Case:** ML models for embedded devices
- **Directory:** `pose_estimate_py/` (external project reference)

#### 4. Blender Integration
- **Technology:** MCP server for Blender
- **Use Case:** 3D modeling via LLM commands
- **Directory:** `blender_mcp/` (referenced in AGENTS.md)
- **Current:** `lav/src/blender_cv/` - Pose estimation for Blender

#### 5. Knowledge Graphs
- **Technology:** Local graph databases
- **Use Case:** Semantic reasoning and knowledge retrieval

#### 6. Web/ML Studio
- **Technology:** LLM Studio with llama.cpp
- **Use Case:** Web-based machine learning interface
- **Directory:** `home/sabeiro/`

### MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

This environment provides MCP server capabilities for interacting with:

| System | Directory | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| Blender | `blender_mcp/` | 3D modeling controls |
| FEM | `heat_fem/` | Finite element calculations |
| Optimization | `phys_opt/` | Energy optimization |
| CV | `pose_estimate_py/` | Computer vision models |
| KB | Knowledge graphs | Local knowledge base |

### Docker Support

Docker containerization for portable deployment:

**Dockerfile** (`home/sabeiro/Dockerfile`)
- Python 3.10 base image
- LLM Studio installation
- llama.cpp integration
- Non-root user for security
- Exposes port 8000 for web interface

**Build & Run Commands:**

```bash
# Build Docker image
docker build -t llm_studio_llama .

# Run container
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama

# Access web interface
# Open http://localhost:8000 in browser
```

### Ollama Setup

The environment includes:
- **Containerized Ollama** for local LLM serving
- **Model management** via `model_list.txt`
- **Direct HF URL downloads** (no token required for public models)
- **Compatible models:**
  - llama-3.1-8b-instruct
  - llama-3.2-3b-instruct
  - llama-3.3-70b-instruct
  - mistral-7b-v0.3
  - phi-3-mini-4k
  - qwen2.5-7b-instruct

### Emacs Integration

Emacs configuration for org-mode based development workflows:
- **Location:** `./emacs/`
- **Workflow:** Code execution via Python REPL and org-mode code blocks
- **Purpose:** Interactive data analytics without production code

## Deployment Options

### 1. Local Development
- Run directly on Ubuntu system
- Use docker-compose for service orchestration
- Accessible via localhost:8000

### 2. Remote Deployment (Jetson)
- **Tool:** Ansible playbooks in `ansible/`
- **Target:** NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Developer Kit
- **Capabilities:** 8GB RAM, ARM Cortex-A55 cores

### 3. Web Server
- **Location:** `nginx/` for web deployment
- **Purpose:** Deploy on Jetson or other servers

### 4. Monitoring
- **Tool:** MCP Hub in `mcphub/`
- **Purpose:** Monitor MCP applications

## Directory Structure

```
/home/sabeiro/
├── home/sabeiro/
│   ├── Dockerfile              # Main Docker build file
│   └── README_llm_studio.md   # LLM Studio specific docs
├── .pi/
│   ├── agent/                  # Pi coding agent configuration
│   │   ├── AGENTS.md          # Agent instructions
│   │   ├── config.json        # Agent configuration
│   │   ├── models.json        # Model list
│   │   └── settings.json      # Agent settings
│   ├── config.json            # Pi coding agent config
│   ├── llama-server.json      # Llama server config
│   ├── mcp_server.json        # MCP server config
│   ├── models.list            # Available models
│   ├── ollama.env             # Ollama environment
│   └── setup.txt              # Setup instructions
├── .ollama/                   # Ollama models and cache
├── .npm/                      # Node packages
├── Dockerfile                 # System container
├── docker-compose.yml         # Service orchestrator
└── pi-session-*.html          # Session logs
```

## Usage Examples

### Starting LLM Studio
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama
```

### Training a Model
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./data:/app/data \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.train.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Running with Ollama
```bash
# Pull a model
ollama pull llama-3.2-3b-instruct

# Run inference
ollama run llama-3.2-3b-instruct "Hello, how are you?"
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `PORT` | Web server port | 8000 |
| `HOST` | Host to bind | 0.0.0.0 |
| `NUM_GPU_LAYERS` | GPU layers for llama.cpp | -1 (all) |
| `NUM_THREADS` | CPU threads | -1 (all) |
| `MAIN_GPU` | Main GPU | -1 |

### Volume Mounts
| Mount | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `./models` | Store GGUF model files |
| `./uploads` | Training datasets |
| `./cache` | Intermediate files |
| `./logs` | Application logs |

### Ollama Models
Available for download (without HF token):
- llamas, mistral, phi, qwen2.5
- Use `get_gguf_without_token.sh` scripts
- Or use direct HF URLs

## Security

- **Run as non-root user:** App user with restricted permissions
- **Read-only base image:** Where possible
- **Security context:** Docker labels with restricted:privileged=true:FALSE

## Troubleshooting

### Out of Memory
Reduce batch size or number of GPU layers:
```bash
export MAX_JOBS=4
export NUM_GPU_LAYERS=-1
```

### Build Cache Issues
```bash
docker builder prune
docker build --no-cache -t llm_studio_llama .
```

### GPU Support
For CUDA support in Docker:
```bash
FROM python:3.10-cudatoolkit-12.1
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
```

## Resources

- [LLM Studio Documentation](https://llm-studio.ml)
- [llama.cpp GitHub](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)
- [Ollama GitHub](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)
- [FEniCS Documentation](https://fenicsproject.org/)

# project scope

This project allows the running of local agents as supporters. Those agents will be used for supporting the development of FEM/blender integration, energy optimization engines and CV/ML on embedded devices.

- goal :: a local coding assistant
- stack :: IDE: emacs, LLM serve: ollama, OS: ubuntu 26
- workflow :: within emacs, code will be executed via python REPL and .org code blocks
- purpose :: data analytics, no need for production code, simple and readable code, avoid abstraction
- test :: no successful results without testing and documenting
- language :: the project language is English, don't translate
- config :: python programs uses json files as config, run logs will be added to that json and saved into a `runs/` folder for versioning

# project structure

Project structure :

- assistants :: coding assistants
  - [[./agent_call.org][agent_call.org]] :: detailed agent instructions to run this project and to explain it's outpt
  - [[./aider/][aider/]] :: conf files to use with aider
  - [[./config.json][config.json]] :: the pi-coding-agent config file
  - [[./emacs][emacs]] :: conf files for agentic usage of emacs in org mode
- deployment ::
  - [[./ansible/][ansible/]] :: ansible script for remote deployment (i.e. jetson)
  - [[./docker-compose.yml][docker-compose.yml]] :: to start mcp_server and mcp_client
  - [[./logs/][logs/]] :: application outputs for debugging
  - [[./nginx/][nginx/]] :: web server configuration to deploy this project (i.e. on jetson)
  - [[./ollama/][ollama/]] :: ollama container and conf
  - [[./mcphub/][mcphub/]] :: to monitor mcp applications
  - [[./morpheus/][morpheus/]] :: nvidia onnx cybersecurity ML enrichment on cuda
  - [[./test/][test/]] :: collection of script to test the configurations
- apps ::
  - [[./blender_mcp/][blender_mcp]] :: definition of the mcp addon to integrate with blender
  - [[./mcp-client/][mcp-client]] :: app to interact with the mcp-server
  - [[./mcp-server/][mcp-server/]] :: app exposing the mcp tools for the language models mainly consumed by gptel
- context ::
  - [[./doc/][doc/]] :: machine generated documentation of useful components
- presentation ::
  - [[./html/][html]] :: slides and diagrams to present the project
  - [[./icon][icon/]] :: useful icons for the presentation
  - [[./img/][img/]] :: images for the documentation
  - [[./html/js/][js/]] :: javascript for the presentation
  - [[./html/css/][css/]] :: style sheets for professional technical documentation
  - [[./data/][data/]] :: input data like json graphs
  - [[./script/][script/]] :: collection of script to run this project

# agent

- local  :: you are developing local applications for pilot test, no need to over engineer the project
- docker :: the applications run locally or in docker, no need for virtual env

# project outcome

- this project provides agentic support to data scientists. The LLMs run locally with ollama, both on ubuntu with Nvidia GPU
- the data scientists need to build an MCP server to allow their programming to interact with different systems:
  - [[./blender-mcp/][blender-mcp/]] :: blender for 3d modeling
  - [[../heat_fem/][heat_fem/]] :: fenics/doplhin for FEM calculation
  - [[../phys_opt/][phys_opt]] :: optimization engine for graphs

  - knowledge graphs

Web pages should be produced with:

- Audience :: scientific/technical blog
- Theme :: dark, elegant, simple, readable
- Layout :: centered and long sections should be collapsable.
- CSS :: use classes to be addressed in style sheets 
- JS :: minimal usage, ideally none
- images :: centered with a opaque background and some shadow
- headers :: h1, h2,h3... should have similar shades but different and elegant
- navbar :: minimal, few links, elegant, discrete
- printable :: the output should be able to produce pdf, no button
- footer :: put intertino as owner and license [[https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/][CC by-nc-sa]] 

# tech stack

The main libraries:

- python: ollama, mcp
- js: d3.js
- web: html/css

# Local AI Development Environment

## Overview

This is a comprehensive local AI development environment designed for data analytics, FEM/Blender integration, energy optimization engines, and computer vision/ML applications on embedded devices.

The project runs local LLMs via Ollama and provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support for various systems including:
- Blender for 3D modeling
- FEniCS/Dolphin for finite element calculations  
- Graph optimization engines
- Computer vision (pose estimation)
- Knowledge graphs

## System Specifications

### Operating System
- **Distro:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat)
- **Kernel:** 7.0.0-22-generic

### CPU
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Model** | AMD Ryzen 7 260 w/ Radeon 780M Graphics |
| **Cores** | 8 physical cores (16 threads with SMT) |
| **Architecture** | Zen 3 (Family 25, Model 117) |
| **Base Frequency** | Variable (417 - 5102 MHz boost) |
| **L1 Cache** | 256 KiB per core (8 instances) |
| **L2 Cache** | 8 MiB (8 instances) |
| **L3 Cache** | 16 MiB (shared) |
| **Virtualization** | AMD-V enabled |

### GPU / Display
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **GPU Model** | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 |
| **CUDA Version** | 13.2 |
| **Driver Version** | 595.71.05 |
| **VRAM** | 8 GiB (GDDR6) |
| **PCIe Device** | 00000000:01:00.0 |

### Memory
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Total RAM** | 30 GiB |
| **Available** | ~14 GiB |
| **Swap** | 11 GiB |

### Storage
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Total Size** | 761 GiB |
| **Used** | 610 GiB (85%) |
| **Available** | 113 GiB |
| **Filesystem** | overlay |

## Software Stack

### AI/ML Stack
- **Ollama:** ✓ Installed (local LLM serving)
- **CUDA:** ✓ Version 13.2
- **NVIDIA Drivers:** ✓ 595.71.05

### Development Tools
- **Python:** For AI/ML development (Python 3.10)
- **GCC/Clang:** For embedded development
- **Ansible:** For remote deployment (Jetson)
- **Docker:** For containerized services
- **FastAPI:** For web APIs
- **Gradio:** For web-based UI

## Project Components

### Main Development Areas

#### 1. FEM Analysis
- **Technology:** FEniCS, Dolphin
- **Use Case:** Heat transfer calculations
- **Directory:** `heat_fem/` (external project reference)

#### 2. Optimization Engine
- **Technology:** Graph-based optimization
- **Use Case:** Energy systems optimization
- **Directory:** `phys_opt/` (external project reference)

#### 3. Computer Vision
- **Technology:** Pose estimation, PyTorch vision models
- **Use Case:** ML models for embedded devices
- **Directory:** `pose_estimate_py/` (external project reference)

#### 4. Blender Integration
- **Technology:** MCP server for Blender
- **Use Case:** 3D modeling via LLM commands
- **Directory:** `blender_mcp/` (referenced in AGENTS.md)
- **Current:** `lav/src/blender_cv/` - Pose estimation for Blender

#### 5. Knowledge Graphs
- **Technology:** Local graph databases
- **Use Case:** Semantic reasoning and knowledge retrieval

#### 6. Web/ML Studio
- **Technology:** LLM Studio with llama.cpp
- **Use Case:** Web-based machine learning interface
- **Directory:** `home/sabeiro/`

### MCP (Model Context Protocol) Support

This environment provides MCP server capabilities for interacting with:

| System | Directory | Description |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| Blender | `blender_mcp/` | 3D modeling controls |
| FEM | `heat_fem/` | Finite element calculations |
| Optimization | `phys_opt/` | Energy optimization |
| CV | `pose_estimate_py/` | Computer vision models |
| KB | Knowledge graphs | Local knowledge base |

### Docker Support

Docker containerization for portable deployment:

**Dockerfile** (`home/sabeiro/Dockerfile`)
- Python 3.10 base image
- LLM Studio installation
- llama.cpp integration
- Non-root user for security
- Exposes port 8000 for web interface

**Build & Run Commands:**

```bash
# Build Docker image
docker build -t llm_studio_llama .

# Run container
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama

# Access web interface
# Open http://localhost:8000 in browser
```

### Ollama Setup

The environment includes:
- **Containerized Ollama** for local LLM serving
- **Model management** via `model_list.txt`
- **Direct HF URL downloads** (no token required for public models)
- **Compatible models:**
  - llama-3.1-8b-instruct
  - llama-3.2-3b-instruct
  - llama-3.3-70b-instruct
  - mistral-7b-v0.3
  - phi-3-mini-4k
  - qwen2.5-7b-instruct

### Emacs Integration

Emacs configuration for org-mode based development workflows:
- **Location:** `./emacs/`
- **Workflow:** Code execution via Python REPL and org-mode code blocks
- **Purpose:** Interactive data analytics without production code

## Deployment Options

### 1. Local Development
- Run directly on Ubuntu system
- Use docker-compose for service orchestration
- Accessible via localhost:8000

### 2. Remote Deployment (Jetson)
- **Tool:** Ansible playbooks in `ansible/`
- **Target:** NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Developer Kit
- **Capabilities:** 8GB RAM, ARM Cortex-A55 cores

### 3. Web Server
- **Location:** `nginx/` for web deployment
- **Purpose:** Deploy on Jetson or other servers

### 4. Monitoring
- **Tool:** MCP Hub in `mcphub/`
- **Purpose:** Monitor MCP applications

## Directory Structure

```
/home/sabeiro/
├── home/sabeiro/
│   ├── Dockerfile              # Main Docker build file
│   └── README_llm_studio.md   # LLM Studio specific docs
├── .pi/
│   ├── agent/                  # Pi coding agent configuration
│   │   ├── AGENTS.md          # Agent instructions
│   │   ├── config.json        # Agent configuration
│   │   ├── models.json        # Model list
│   │   └── settings.json      # Agent settings
│   ├── config.json            # Pi coding agent config
│   ├── llama-server.json      # Llama server config
│   ├── mcp_server.json        # MCP server config
│   ├── models.list            # Available models
│   ├── ollama.env             # Ollama environment
│   └── setup.txt              # Setup instructions
├── .ollama/                   # Ollama models and cache
├── .npm/                      # Node packages
├── Dockerfile                 # System container
├── docker-compose.yml         # Service orchestrator
└── pi-session-*.html          # Session logs
```

## Usage Examples

### Starting LLM Studio
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    -v ./uploads:/app/uploads \
    -v ./cache:/app/cache \
    --name llm_studio \
    llm_studio_llama
```

### Training a Model
```bash
docker run -d \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    -v ./data:/app/data \
    -v ./models:/app/models \
    llm_studio_llama \
    python -m llm_studio.train.cli \
    --port 8000 \
    --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Running with Ollama
```bash
# Pull a model
ollama pull llama-3.2-3b-instruct

# Run inference
ollama run llama-3.2-3b-instruct "Hello, how are you?"
```

## Configuration

### Environment Variables
| Variable | Description | Default |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| `PORT` | Web server port | 8000 |
| `HOST` | Host to bind | 0.0.0.0 |
| `NUM_GPU_LAYERS` | GPU layers for llama.cpp | -1 (all) |
| `NUM_THREADS` | CPU threads | -1 (all) |
| `MAIN_GPU` | Main GPU | -1 |

### Volume Mounts
| Mount | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `./models` | Store GGUF model files |
| `./uploads` | Training datasets |
| `./cache` | Intermediate files |
| `./logs` | Application logs |

### Ollama Models
Available for download (without HF token):
- llamas, mistral, phi, qwen2.5
- Use `get_gguf_without_token.sh` scripts
- Or use direct HF URLs

## Security

- **Run as non-root user:** App user with restricted permissions
- **Read-only base image:** Where possible
- **Security context:** Docker labels with restricted:privileged=true:FALSE

## Troubleshooting

### Out of Memory
Reduce batch size or number of GPU layers:
```bash
export MAX_JOBS=4
export NUM_GPU_LAYERS=-1
```

### Build Cache Issues
```bash
docker builder prune
docker build --no-cache -t llm_studio_llama .
```

### GPU Support
For CUDA support in Docker:
```bash
FROM python:3.10-cudatoolkit-12.1
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
```

## Resources

- [LLM Studio Documentation](https://llm-studio.ml)
- [llama.cpp GitHub](https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp)
- [Ollama GitHub](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)
- [FEniCS Documentation](https://fenicsproject.org/)
